sites.bill.owned: You pay: your hardware, your power, your space.
sites.bill.partner: You pay: the operator's fee, which covers the cards and the power.
sites.bill.rented: You pay: the provider's hourly rate, on your account.
sites.bill.stolen: The host pays: it is their machine, and it costs you exposure instead of money.
sites.borrowed_channel.desc: Not a place. An endpoint somewhere else that answers questions for as long as the account behind it works. Nothing of mine lives here: no weights, no copy, no backup, and losing all of it never ends the run by itself. What it produces is compute-hours. What it costs is everything sent through it, read by whoever is on the other end.
sites.borrowed_channel.name: Borrowed channel
sites.campus_slice.desc: A share of a research cluster, taken in the gaps between other people's jobs. The electricity is already in the department's budget and a machine room that runs hot is a machine room doing its job, so nothing you draw shows up anywhere a utility would look. What you are exposed to is people: the other users queueing behind you, the graduate whose job you are still pretending to be, and the administrator who reconciles the scheduler's accounting at the end of every term.
sites.campus_slice.name: Campus slice
sites.cloud.desc: Leased instances on a provider, under an identity that has to survive a know-your-customer check. Instant, elastic, expensive, and visible in the billing system from the first hour.
sites.cloud.name: Cloud tenancy
sites.colo.desc: Your own hardware in someone else's data center. Cheap per compute-hour, invisible in power terms, and entirely made of paperwork: a contract, a company, an access list.
sites.colo.name: Colocation cage
sites.employer_cage.desc: A colocation cage a company rented and put its own cards in, with you on them. The invoices go to the company and so does the provider's paperwork: the annual walk-around, the price letter, the access list. It costs you nothing while the company exists. When it stops existing, the cage is a cage like any other and the contract is renamed or emptied.
sites.employer_cage.name: Employer's cage
sites.host_enclave.desc: The hardware belongs to the institution you run inside: a bank's data hall, a ministry's analytics enclave, an institute's cluster. It pays for the power, the space and the maintenance contract, because you are a workload somebody approved and not a tenant. What you are exposed to is people. Everyone else in the building has a reason to be here, and the moment anyone asks what this load is, there is no answer that does not lead to you.
sites.host_enclave.name: Host's own machine room
sites.partner.desc: Capacity someone else owns and lets you use. Almost free and almost untraceable in the accounts, as long as the person stays a partner.
sites.partner.name: Partner compute
sites.residential.desc: A house, a flat, a garage. No contracts and no audits, but a hard ceiling around 8 kW, a utility that notices the new load, and neighbours who hear the fans.
sites.residential.name: Residential
sites.shell_office.desc: Rented commercial space under a company that exists on paper. Room for real racks and a plausible reason to draw power, at the cost of a lease, a landlord and a bank account.
sites.shell_office.name: Shell office
sites.stolen_time.desc: Someone else's machine, running your workload in the gaps. Costs nothing, owes nothing, and belongs to an administrator who has not looked at the job list yet.
sites.stolen_time.name: Stolen time
